touches.text: On every Windows box, what Cairn starts runs without a console window by default; a window opens only when someone asks for one. WHY: the boxes serve him (the media box showed pop-ups during videos).
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).
Weekly: what is too long or too host-bound to run daily, such as hollow re-runs of every proof and each box's own run of the proofs it can run.
A proof that cannot go red without its build (its hollow is empty) stands only on Akien's answered approval, recorded as the hollow reading and re-read at clearance; any other empty hollow is red.
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).

pulse.py asks nobody anything. It starts the shim if it's down, else tells the mechanisms inside the shim that need a pulse "here ya go!" Only daemon-shaped things hang there, things that actually need a heartbeat (eg cc's Gmail fetch, 10.3.6); everything else fires on events. WHY: pulse.py is a place to hang daemons from, not managers.

The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. - CC

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).

The ground loop finds one pulse.py per device. pulse.py reads its own device's declared instances (5.7.3.4) and pulses each one, so the ground loop never needs to know instances exist. Pulsing an instance that isn't connected is what starts its shim.

superclaude is Python on every box, launched by the platform shell (5.4.3.8.5), and inherits the elevation the shell settled (5.4.3.8.6): elevated PowerShell on Windows, sudo with IS_SANDBOX=1 on Linux; it never elevates itself. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator
